text: One extra meter around Earth. Could a cat crawl under?
Wrap a rope tight around the whole Earth.
Now make it just one meter longer.
Lift it evenly, all the way around.
How big is the gap? Pause and guess.
One meter, spread around forty thousand kilometers, sounds like nothing.
But the gap is about sixteen centimeters.
That is enough for a cat to crawl under.
A rope lifted one step gets about six steps longer.
So one extra meter lifts it about a sixth of a meter.
And the size of the ball never matters.
Around a tennis ball, it is the same sixteen centimeters.
